attributes:
# R34: line endings. Git for Windows checks text out as CRLF by default (core.autocrlf=true), and on a
# real Windows 11 checkout that broke three things: 94 of the 213 hashes in tests/negative/r17/SHA256SUMS,
# tools/r69_build.py --check-only (it hashes the raw bytes against the pins), and one program the Linux
# compiler refused because the CR bytes pushed it over its source limit. The committed bytes are LF; these
# rules only make every checkout match them. No file's content changes.

# Sources: always LF.
*.sm        text eol=lf
*.smlib     text eol=lf
*.asm       text eol=lf
*.inc       text eol=lf
*.lang      text eol=lf
*.sandesh   text eol=lf
*.sffi      text eol=lf

# Test data and goldens: the exact committed bytes, never converted (their hashes and goldens are bytes).
tests/negative/**   -text
tests/expect/**     -text

# Evidence typed in the Windows IDE: kept as recorded (CRLF).
Claude-to-Sarvam/evidence-r9/wine/*.sm   -text
source: Checked-in release package obtained from this Windows checkout; not a new Windows build
